statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation of the multivariate Taylor expansion (the 'Proofs' section begins with 'Proof for Taylor's theorem in one real variable' and truncates at 'Let'). As stated in the sources, if f: R^n -> R is k + 1 times continuously differentiable in a closed ball B = {y in R^n : ||a - y|| <= r} for some r > 0, the multivariate Taylor expansion of f about a is given by f(x) = sum_{|alpha| <= k} (D^alpha f(a) / alpha!) (x - a)^alpha + sum_{|beta| = k+1} R_beta(x) (x - a)^beta, where R_beta(x) = (|beta| / beta!) int_0^1 (1 - t)^{|beta| - 1} D^beta f(a + t(x - a)) dt.

symbols.meaning: argument vector at which f is approximated
center point of the Taylor expansion
order of the Taylor polynomial approximation
sum of the components of multi-index alpha (alpha_1 + ... + alpha_n)
higher-order partial derivative partial^{|alpha|} f / (partial x_1^{alpha_1} ... partial x_n^{alpha_n})
exact remainder coefficient function for multi-index beta
closed ball {y in R^n : ||a - y|| <= r}
radius of the closed ball B
parameter of integration along the line segment between a and x

properties.property: Uniform estimate on the remainder: |R_beta(x)| <= (1 / beta!) * max_{|alpha| = |beta|} max_{y in B} |D^alpha f(y)| for all x in B.
properties.why: Follows from the integral formula for R_beta(x) and the continuity of the (k+1)-th order partial derivatives on the compact ball B.

properties.property: Third-order expansion formula in two dimensions (n = 2, k = 3): for v = x - a, P_3(x) = f(a) + (partial f / partial x_1)(a) v_1 + (partial f / partial x_2)(a) v_2 + (partial^2 f / partial x_1^2)(a) (v_1^2 / 2!) + (partial^2 f / partial x_1 partial x_2)(a) v_1 v_2 + (partial^2 f / partial x_2^2)(a) (v_2^2 / 2!) + (partial^3 f / partial x_1^3)(a) (v_1^3 / 3!) + (partial^3 f / partial x_1^2 partial x_2)(a) (v_1^2 v_2 / 2!) + (partial^3 f / partial x_1 partial x_2^2)(a) (v_1 v_2^2 / 2!) + (partial^3 f / partial x_2^3)(a) (v_2^3 / 3!).
properties.why: Specializes the multi-index Taylor sum to dimension 2 up to degree 3.

properties.property: Justification of multi-index derivative notation D^alpha f: the order of mixed partial derivatives at a can be changed arbitrarily.
properties.why: Follows from Clairaut's theorem because all k-th order partial derivatives of f are continuous at a.

properties.property: First-order differential formula: df(a)(v) = (partial f / partial x_1)(a) v_1 + ... + (partial f / partial x_n)(a) v_n.
properties.why: Follows from the definition of differentiability f(x) = f(a) + L(x - a) + h(x)||x - a|| with lim_{x -> a} h(x) = 0 and L = df(a).

assumptions.assumption: f: R^n -> R is k + 1 times continuously differentiable in a closed ball B = {y in R^n : ||a - y|| <= r} for some r > 0.
assumptions.breaks_when: Any (k+1)-th order partial derivative of f does not exist or fails to be continuous on B.

assumptions.assumption: The evaluation point x lies within the closed ball B centered at a of radius r.
All k-th order partial derivatives of f are continuous at a (or (k-1)-th order partial derivatives exist in a neighborhood of a and are differentiable at a).
assumptions.breaks_when: Discontinuity of k-th order partial derivatives causes Clairaut's theorem to fail, making mixed partial derivatives dependent on differentiation order.

failure_modes.mode: Invalid remainder bound or undefined remainder integral
failure_modes.signature: R_beta(x) fails to satisfy the uniform bound (1 / beta!) * max_{|alpha| = |beta|} max_{y in B} |D^alpha f(y)| or the integral diverges.
failure_modes.cause: (k+1)-th order partial derivatives are discontinuous or unbounded along the segment between a and x, or x is outside B.

failure_modes.mode: Ambiguous derivative operators in multi-index sum
failure_modes.signature: D^alpha f(a) is not well-defined, yielding differing values depending on the order of differentiation.
failure_modes.cause: Clairaut's theorem fails when the k-th order partial derivatives are not continuous at a.

failure_modes.mode: Taylor series divergence from function values
failure_modes.signature: The sum of the infinite Taylor series does not equal f(x) even if the series converges.
failure_modes.cause: The function f is not analytic at a, despite being infinitely differentiable.

canon_notes: multivariate_taylor_expansion is statement-tier, so its statement is what the canon asks for; the source's proof section was not required
